subject: Mathematics

source.topic: Data handling: Analyse and interpret data

show.line: This pictograph shows the weather this month. Each sun picture is one sunny day. Count the suns!

rounds.prompt: Count the suns. How many sunny days?
Which weather happened the least this month?
Six rainy days and nine sunny days. How many more sunny days? Say the number.
Here are the fruit sold today. Which fruit sold the most?
rounds.praise: Yes! The banana row is the longest.

rounds.prompt: Each picture stands for two children. Three pictures for netball. How many children? Tap the number.
rounds.praise: Yes! Three pictures of two is six children.

rounds.story: The graph shows four children chose red, seven chose blue and two chose green. Which colour did most children choose?

hints: Count the pictures in each row. More pictures means more.
Check the key. One picture might stand for more than one.

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! I will find the fruit that sold the least.
beat_the_tutor.tutor_try: Bananas! The banana row is the longest, so it is the least!
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! The longest row is the most. The shortest row, pears, is the least.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's look together. The shortest row has the fewest. Pears!

parent_line: Can read a pictograph and answer questions about it.
